title: Hotmail launched on 4 July 1996.
description:
Hotmail launched on 4 July 1996. Sabeer Bhatia and Jack Smith had pitched a free web email service to Draper Fisher Jurvetson in 1995. The firm wondered how they would attract members.

Tim Draper wanted every email to carry an advert. He suggested a plug at the bottom of every outgoing message. The founders resisted, then agreed to the plug but not the P.S. I love you part.

The line everyone quotes may not be what shipped. TechCrunch says the founders dropped the P.S. I love you wording. Another account says that exact line was appended for years. The sources disagree.

Subscribers in the first year and a half, on less than $500,000 of marketing, according to Jurvetson and Draper's Viral Marketing article.

The first million took about six months. TechCrunch's excerpt from Viral Loop says Hotmail reached 1 million users within six months of launch.

By February 1999 Hotmail had more than 30 million active members. Microsoft's own release said new sign ups frequently topped 1 million a week.

Every email sent was an advert for the service.

Sources:
- https://news.microsoft.com/1999/02/08/msn-hotmail-from-zero-to-30-million-members-in-30-months/: read. Established the 4 July 1996 launch, that Bhatia and Smith approached Draper Fisher Jurvetson in 1995, that the firm wondered how they would attract members, more than 30 million active members by February 1999, and a sign up rate frequently above 1 million a week.
- https://techcrunch.com/2009/10/18/ps-i-love-you-get-your-free-email-at-hotmail: read. Established that Tim Draper pushed for a plug at the bottom of every outgoing email, that the founders resisted, that they later agreed but without the P.S. I love you part, and that Hotmail reached 1 million users within six months. This is an excerpt from Adam Penenberg's book Viral Loop.
- https://steve.blog/2013/10/23/red-herring-hotmail-photoshoot-for-the-original-viral-marketing-article/: read. Reprints Steve Jurvetson and Tim Draper's Viral Marketing article. Established that Tim Draper suggested appending an advert to every outbound email, that Hotmail signed up over 12 million subscribers in its first 1.5 years, and that it spent less than $500,000 on marketing from launch to 12 million users.
- https://www.webmaster-source.com/2009/10/22/a-brief-history-of-hotmail-or-an-example-of-early-viral-marketing/: read. Established an account in which a line reading PS: I love you. Get your free e-mail at Hotmail was appended for years, which conflicts with the TechCrunch excerpt.
